Understanding asynchronous Rust

Tokio is an asynchronous runtime for Rust. It schedules tasks while they wait for network operations, allowing an application to serve other requests without creating a new operating system thread for every connection. This makes concurrent I/O practical for a page reader that downloads articles and streams model responses.

Bound the work

Concurrency still needs limits. A server should limit active downloads, memory consumed by response bodies, and requests to external providers. Slow clients and slow websites must not be allowed to consume all available capacity. CPU-intensive parsing belongs in a separate, bounded worker pool.

Cancellation drops network work when a reader disconnects. Requests that have started generating model output should not be retried automatically, because another request may create another charge. A clear user-controlled retry keeps this behavior understandable.
